statement: Finiteness of exceptions inherits obstruction from CL-10: cannot be proved without resolving the key inequality

premises.note: CL-10 (key inequality) is OBL with recorded obstruction; finiteness of exceptions depends on the key inequality
E_eps = {(a,b,c) coprime, a+b=c : c > K_eps * rad(abc)^(1+eps)}. Finiteness of E_eps is exactly the abc conjecture for this eps.

proof_steps.label: finiteness-follows-from-key-inequality
proof_steps.claim: If the key inequality c <= K_eps * rad(abc)^(1+eps) holds for all but finitely many coprime triples, then E_eps is finite by definition.
proof_steps.justification: The exception set E_eps is exactly the set of triples violating the key inequality. If P_ineq holds universally (or with finitely many exceptions), then E_eps has at most those finitely many exceptions. This is a logical tautology: finiteness of E_eps is equivalent to the key inequality holding for all but finitely many triples.

proof_steps.label: finiteness-is-abc
proof_steps.claim: Finiteness of E_eps for all eps > 0 IS the abc conjecture (without the quantitative bound K_eps).
proof_steps.justification: The abc conjecture states: for all eps > 0, |E_eps| < infinity. Proving finiteness of E_eps without the quantitative bound K_eps is not weaker than abc — it is equivalent to it (the bound K_eps and finiteness are interchangeable in the definition). Therefore any proof of CL-11 that does not use abc as a hypothesis must also provide a proof of the quantitative bound.

proof_steps.label: independent-finiteness-not-known
proof_steps.claim: No proof of |E_eps| < infinity is known that does not assume abc or an abc-equivalent assertion.
proof_steps.justification: By step 2, proving |E_eps| < infinity independently IS a proof of abc. Since abc is an open problem, no such proof exists. Faltings' theorem (CL-05) gives finiteness for fixed curves of genus >= 2 but does NOT give uniform finiteness over all coprime triples. The finiteness claimed in P_finiteness must be uniform.

proof_steps.label: obstruction-conclusion
proof_steps.claim: CL-11 (finiteness proved uniformly without abc-equivalent input) remains OPEN. The obstruction is inherited from CL-10.
proof_steps.justification: Steps 1-3 show that CL-11 is equivalent to CL-10 in difficulty: any proof of finiteness requires either the key inequality (step 1, which requires CL-10) or directly provides an abc proof (step 2-3, which violates B2). The obstruction is precisely recorded.

resolution_required: Resolution of CL-10 (the key inequality obstruction) automatically resolves CL-11
Alternatively: a direct proof of uniform finiteness that does not use abc as hypothesis (which would also resolve CL-10)
non_circularity: No abc assumed; finiteness of exceptions IS the abc conjecture without the quantitative bound. This record documents the precise dependency on CL-10.
